lane: A6 — the arcade leaderboard showed his brother nothing
owner_item: His brother finished a NONET, typed his name, and the board showed nobody else — although the owner had played several runs the day before and expected a populated board.
root_cause:
THE BOARD IS SERVER-BACKED ONLY IF A BUILD-TIME STRING SURVIVED THE BUILD, AND EVERY WAY IT CAN FAIL IS SILENT AND INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM EVERY OTHER WAY.

H1 (the reveal gate did not open) is REFUTED IN CODE. The gate is `ArcadeRun.update`, populated only by `applyUpdate`, which only `submitRun` reaches (`src/render/arcadeRun.ts:172-175`, `:190-211`); `main.ts:1459-1486` drives it on ENTER and `main.ts:1495-1499` is the only door to `BOARD`. If it had not opened he would have seen no table at all; he saw a table with one name. The gate worked. Do not touch it — it is R182-G, canon §9, anti-griefing.

H2 IS THE LIVE QUESTION AND THE ANSWER IS CONDITIONAL. The storage tier is the browser: `arcadeScores.ts:310` reads `globalThis.localStorage?.getItem(rankingKeyFor(boardId))`, key `spark.arcade.nonet.ranking.v1` (`:70-72`) — per browser profile, per machine. The shared tier is selected by exactly one expression, `arcadeLeaderboard.ts:489`: `return base === '' ? new LocalLeaderboard() : new RemoteLeaderboard(base);`, where `base` is `REMOTE_BASE` = `parseLeaderboardBase(import.meta.env.VITE_LEADERBOARD_URL ?? '')` (`:469`), inlined at BUILD time by `vite.config.ts:51-54` from the repo variable in `deploy.yml:194`. **So if that variable did not reach the CI build that produced the live bundle, the game is `localStorage`-only and his brother on another machine correctly sees an empty board — the feature is simply not shared, exactly as it was before S182.** That cannot be settled from the tree; it is a property of the deployed asset. See the probe.

AND WHETHER OR NOT THE URL SHIPPED, THREE CODE-LEVEL DEFECTS ARE CONFIRMED AND EACH ALONE PRODUCES THIS REPORT:

(1) EVERY SERVER FAILURE COLLAPSES TO "OFFLINE" WITH NO SIGNAL. `arcadeLeaderboard.ts:359` is `if (!res.ok) return null;` and `:388-390` catches everything else — a 403 bad origin, a 404 unknown board, a 500 from a missing D1 table, a 503 for an unset `IP_SALT`, a captive portal, a 4 s abort and a genuinely dead network all return the same `null` and fall to the local tier. The ONLY thing on screen is an 18px grey caption at `arcadeRunOverlay.ts:306`: `'this device only · by average time'` versus `'everyone · by average time'`. Nothing says a submission was refused, nothing says it was queued, nothing says why. The owner cannot tell the fix from the bug, which is the exact failure `scripts/leaderboard-wiring-report.mjs:11-13` was written to prevent on the CI side and nobody wrote on the player side.

(2) THE SERVER IS VERSIONED BY A HUMAN'S SHELL HISTORY, AND TWO SCHEMA MIGRATIONS LIVE ONLY IN A FILE SOMEBODY HAS TO RUN. `.github/workflows/e2e.yml:543` states it: the worker *"runs on Cloudflare, ships by `wrangler deploy`"*. Nothing in `.github/` and no script in `package.json:7-28` deploys it or applies `schema.sql`. Since the go-live commit `e1fe909` (2026-09-18 19:37) the data model was rebuilt twice: `24d5a41` (20:52) replaced the per-run `scores` table with `players`, and `41b0da6` (22:55) added `seen_runs`. ⛔ **If `seen_runs` was never created on the live D1, every real browser submit 500s while a curl passes**: `arcadeLeaderboard.ts:296` mints an id for every run and `:354` sends `id` on every one, so `worker.js:412` `const ids = runs.map((r) => r.id).filter((id) => id !== null)` is always non-empty and `:414-419` always runs `SELECT id FROM seen_runs WHERE id IN (…)`. A hand-rolled curl sends no id, `ids.length` is 0, the SELECT is skipped and the INSERT is filtered out at `:434-435` — so the *"Verified live"* claims in `41b0da6`'s own commit message could not have touched that table. That is a perfect blind spot, and `src/server.worker.test.ts:24` `function makeDb(...)` is an in-memory mock that answers every SQL string, so the 5289-test suite is green whatever the live D1 contains.

(3) HIS RUNS FROM "YESTERDAY" ARE ALREADY GONE FROM THE QUEUE, BY THE CODE'S OWN ARITHMETIC. If the remote tier was configured and his POSTs failed, each run was queued (`arcadeLeaderboard.ts:300-305`) stamped `at: Date.now()` (`:296`), and `prunePending` (`arcadeScores.ts:422-427`) drops anything older than `PENDING_MAX_AGE_MS` = 12 h (`:401`). He played the evening of 09-18; 12 h expired the morning of 09-19. **His next submit will silently bin them and they will never reach the shared board** — his local average keeps them, the world's does not. Canon §9's caveat already names the cheap fix (raise `SEEN_RUN_TTL_MS`, `worker.js:95`), and it was not taken because S183 was scoped client-side only.

H4 is mostly NOT the cause — there is no min-runs filter and ranking is from run 1, exactly as R182-G requires (`arcadeScores.ts:176-178`, `worker.js:179-190`). But two read/write-path losses are real and silent: the server returns `rejected` and `duplicates` (`worker.js:485`) and the client parses neither (`arcadeLeaderboard.ts:362-387`), so a run dropped by the 15 s floor `MIN_MS` (`worker.js:70`) vanishes with no trace; and the 429 arm deliberately returns the board (`worker.js:350`) which `:359`'s `!res.ok` throws away, so that kindness is dead code.

evidence.why_it_matters: THE BOARD'S BASE TIER IS BROWSER STORAGE, per profile and per machine (key `spark.arcade.nonet.ranking.v1`, :70-72). If the shared tier is not selected, his brother on another machine SHOULD see an empty board — that is correct behaviour of a feature that is not actually shared, not a rendering bug.

EVERY server refusal — 403 origin, 404 unknown board, 429 rate limit, 500 missing table, 503 unset IP_SALT — becomes the same `null` as being offline, and `:388-390` catches the rest. The client cannot distinguish a dead backend from a train tunnel, so neither can the owner.

So the entire 5289-test suite is green regardless of what the live database actually contains — the migration gap is structurally invisible to the gates.

He said 'yesterday'. If his runs queued on the evening of 09-18 because the POST failed, `prunePending` (:422-427) expired them the morning of 09-19 — his next submit DROPS them and they never reach the shared board. The timing in his complaint lines up with this constant exactly.

The server reports how many runs it threw away (MIN_MS 15 s floor at :70, MAX_MS 1 h) and how many were duplicates — and the client parses NEITHER (arcadeLeaderboard.ts:362-387 read only `rows` and `you`). A legitimately fast run is discarded from the shared board with nothing on screen.

The runbook's API section still documents the PRE-R182-G per-run shape that was replaced at 24d5a41. Anyone diagnosing this board by following the README will curl the wrong body shape and draw the wrong conclusion — it must be corrected in the same change.

fix_shape:
RUN THE PROBE FIRST — the fix branches on it, and it is 30 seconds. Then, in this order:

A. MAKE THE FAILURE VISIBLE (do this whatever the probe says; it is the reason he could not diagnose it himself). `RemoteLeaderboard.post` returns a discriminated result instead of `null`: `{ok:true, …} | {ok:false, why:'offline'|'refused'|'rate-limited'|'server-error'|'not-configured'}`. `if (!res.ok)` at :359 branches on `res.status` (403/404 → 'refused', 429 → 'rate-limited' and KEEP the rows the server sent at worker.js:350, 5xx → 'server-error'); the catch at :388 stays 'offline'. Add `why: string | null` and `queued: number` to `RankingUpdate` (:81-109). `LocalLeaderboard.submit` reports `'not-configured'`. ~40 lines in `arcadeLeaderboard.ts`.

B. SAY IT ON SCREEN. `arcadeRunOverlay.drawBoard` (~:298-330) gains one line under the existing caption when `shared === false`: 'SAVED ON THIS DEVICE — <n> RUN(S) WAITING TO SYNC' for 'offline', and a distinct line for 'server-error'/'refused' ('THE SHARED BOARD IS NOT ANSWERING'). Add both to the `last` snapshot record (:86) or no test can see them. ~15 lines + the snapshot field.

C. SURFACE WHAT THE SERVER ALREADY TELLS US. Parse `rejected` and `duplicates` in `post` (:362-387) and report a rejected run on the recap ('THIS RUN WAS NOT ACCEPTED — TIME OUTSIDE THE ALLOWED RANGE'). ~12 lines. This is what makes a MIN_MS drop stop being invisible.

D. STOP THE SERVER BEING VERSIONED BY SHELL HISTORY. Add to `package.json`: `"leaderboard:migrate": "wrangler d1 execute spark-leaderboard --remote -y --file=./server/leaderboard/schema.sql"`, `"leaderboard:deploy": "wrangler deploy -c server/leaderboard/wrangler.toml"`, `"probe-leaderboard": "node scripts/probe-leaderboard.mjs"`. New `scripts/probe-leaderboard.mjs` modelled on `scripts/probe-relays.mjs`: POST one run WITH an id against the live worker and print a verdict (healthy / missing table / bad origin / IP_SALT unset / unreachable). ~60 lines. This is the single highest-value artefact here — it is the command that answers 'is the board actually live?' and today no such command exists.

E. STOP DROPPING QUEUED RUNS (canon §9 already blesses this). Raise `SEEN_RUN_TTL_MS` (worker.js:95) 24 h → 7 d and `PENDING_MAX_AGE_MS` (arcadeScores.ts:401) 12 h → 72 h, keeping the inequality `pendingRunExpiry.test.ts` pins. Two constants plus their docblocks; requires a `wrangler deploy` to take effect, which is why D lands first.

F. CORRECT THE README. `server/leaderboard/README.md:168-175` still documents the retired per-run `{"scores":[…]}` API — replace with the live `{runs:[{name,ms,id}], focus}` → `{rows, rejected, duplicates, you:{runs,averageMs,previousAverageMs,place}}` shape.

⛔ DO NOT touch the reveal gate, the average-not-best-time model, name-as-identity, or the sum-and-count storage — all four are canon §9 owner rulings. DO NOT "fix" H1; it is not broken.
determinism_risk:
NONE — SIM-FREE BY CONSTRUCTION, AND THE CODE SAYS SO. `arcadeRun.ts:27-33`: *"an arcade run touches no simulation state, crosses no wire and feeds nothing host-authoritative. `world.sudoku` stays `null` for the entire run."* No hashed entity gains a field, so there is NO four-sites obligation (no factory, no serialize, no `hashWorldState`/`hashWorldStateFull`, no worker). Nothing crosses the peer wire, so **PROTOCOL_VERSION stays 47** — do not bump it.

Two wall-clock/entropy uses are already inside this module and are LEGITIMATE because they are outside the tick, but a fix must not migrate either into sim code: `Date.now()` at `arcadeScores.ts:296` (the `at` stamp), `:363` (the backfill), `:426` (`prunePending`), and `Math.random()` in the `newRunId` fallback at `arcadeScores.ts:145`. Keep `prunePending(pending, now)` taking `now` as a parameter so it stays pure and testable — that is what `pendingRunExpiry.test.ts` relies on.

⚠ Map-iteration order: not in play. The ranking is a total order already (`compareRows`, `arcadeScores.ts:169-173` — average, then runs DESC, then name) and is mirrored exactly in `worker.js:179-190` and the SQL at `worker.js:470-477`. **If any ordering is touched, all THREE must move together or a player's stated place disagrees with the row they are looking at.**

⚠ Doc drift found in passing, free to fix: `The Spark/CLAUDE.md` § "Protocol version" still says `PROTOCOL_VERSION` is **46**; `SPARK_CANON.md` §9b and the S182 handoff both say **47**.
tests_owed:
RED BEFORE, GREEN AFTER:

1. `src/render/arcadeLeaderboard.test.ts` — a stubbed `fetch` answering 500, 403, 404 and 429 must each yield a distinct `why` on the `RankingUpdate`, and the 429 case must still carry the rows the server sent. Today all four are indistinguishable from offline at `arcadeLeaderboard.ts:359`, so the assertion cannot even be written.
2. `src/render/arcadeLeaderboard.test.ts` — a 200 whose body carries `rejected: 1` must surface it. Today `:362-387` never reads the field.
3. `src/render/arcadeRunOverlay.test.ts` — with `update.shared === false`, the BOARD screen's snapshot must contain the new sync line, and with `why === 'server-error'` a different one. ⚠ **NO RENDERER RUNS UNDER VITEST** — this suite reads the overlay's `last` snapshot object (`arcadeRunOverlay.ts:86`, written at `:135` and `:174`), never drawn pixels, so a new on-screen line is invisible to the suite unless it is ALSO recorded into that snapshot. That is the pin; there is no e2e lane covering the arcade board at all (`e2e:gating` and `e2e:races` cover neither).
4. `src/server.worker.test.ts` — a `db` whose `prepare` throws `no such table: seen_runs` must produce a response the client can tell apart from a generic failure. The shape already exists at `:199` for `players` (`throw new Error('no such table: players')`) — extend it, and assert the id-carrying path is the one that reaches the SELECT (i.e. a no-id batch must NOT touch `seen_runs`), which is the blind spot itself, pinned.
5. `src/render/pendingRunExpiry.test.ts` — re-pin `PENDING_MAX_AGE_MS < SEEN_RUN_TTL_MS` against the worker's EXPORTED constant after the raise in fix E. It already imports the real constant; the literal must be derived, not re-typed (the S177 rule).
6. `src/ci.leaderboardGate.test.ts` — NEW source-text pin: `package.json` carries a one-command migrate AND deploy path for the worker. ⚠ Per S182 lesson 2 a source-text guard proves a line EXISTS, not that it is REACHED — so pair it with a mechanical enumeration: assert the count of `env.DB.prepare(` call sites in `worker.js` against the set of tables `schema.sql` creates, so a new table added to the worker without a `CREATE TABLE` fails the suite. That is the guard that would have caught this class.
7. `SPARK_CANON.md` §9 gains the server-versioning caveat, with its assertion in `src/canon.test.ts` in the SAME COMMIT if any number lands in it.
owner_ruling_needed: ⛔ DOES A REFUSED SUBMISSION SPEAK, AND HOW LOUDLY? Today it is silent by design — `arcadeLeaderboard.ts:244-248` argues 'the recap is the last thing a player sees after a good run; it is the worst possible place to surface a network error', and that argument is genuinely good. But the cost of it is THIS BUG REPORT: he had no way to tell a fixed board from the original one. OPTION A — one amber line under the ranking caption ('SAVED ON THIS DEVICE — 3 RUNS WAITING TO SYNC'), which costs a little of the arcade's clean payoff screen and ends the ambiguity forever. OPTION B — keep the recap silent and put the state on the TITLE screen instead, where nothing is at stake. OPTION C — keep it as it is and rely on the new probe command. I recommend A: the caption at `arcadeRunOverlay.ts:306` is already trying to say this and is too quiet to work.

⛔ HIS RUNS FROM THE 18th — LET THEM GO, OR BACKFILL THEM? If the probe shows they never reached the server, they exist only in his browser's `spark.arcade.nonet.ranking.v1` key, and by `PENDING_MAX_AGE_MS` (12 h, `arcadeScores.ts:401`) any queued copies are already expired. OPTION A — let them go; his shared average starts from his next run, and canon §9's 'nothing can ever be repaired' stays true without exception. OPTION B — a one-off backfill: read his local `runs`+`totalMs` and fold it in as a single admin POST. That means the board accepts a number typed by a client rather than earned through the floor/ceiling checks, i.e. a deliberate hole in the one anti-cheat this design has, opened for one person. I recommend A, and it costs him maybe five runs of average.

⚠ IS THE 15-SECOND FLOOR EATING REAL RUNS? `MIN_MS = 15_000` (`worker.js:70`) is MINE, not his, justified as '20 deliberate clicks plus digits cannot be done faster by a human'. A NONET is 36 cells with 16 givens (`sudoku.ts:20`, `:54`) — 20 blanks, so the floor assumes no faster than 0.75 s per cell. A run under it is DISCARDED with nothing on screen (the client never reads `rejected`, see fix C). I need ONE number only he has: what does he actually finish a NONET in, at his fastest? If it is anywhere near 20 s the floor should drop to ~8 s, because a floor that silently eats a legitimate record is worse than the accidental zero it was written to stop.
size_estimate: Standard (10-30K) — six production files plus one new script, six test files, and a live diagnosis step; no sim work and no protocol change. ⚠ It tips to Full (>30K) if the owner picks the backfill in ruling 2, or if the fix adds a scheduled CI job that probes the live worker (that would touch `.github/workflows/e2e.yml`, which S182 proved is a shared-infrastructure file five branches will fight over).
blocked_on:
NOT BLOCKED ON HIM TO START — the diagnosis is mechanical and takes 30 seconds. It IS blocked on running the probe before choosing between the branches of the fix, because the tree cannot tell you whether the live bundle carries the worker URL or whether the live D1 has the tables the current worker queries.

⭐ THE ONE PROBE THAT SETTLES IT — STEP 1 (settles H2: is the shipped board shared at all?):

  curl -s https://spark-online.space/ | grep -o 'assets/index-[A-Za-z0-9_-]*\.js'

then, with the filename it prints:

  curl -s https://spark-online.space/assets/<that file> | grep -c 'spark-leaderboard'

A count of **0 means the live bundle has no worker URL**: the board is `localStorage` only, every player is alone on their own machine, his brother's empty board was CORRECT behaviour, and the fix is a repo variable plus a deploy — not a code change. A count of 1 or more means the client is wired and the fault is server-side, so:

⭐ STEP 2 (settles the migration gap — note the `id`, which is the arm a plain curl never exercises and which every real browser submit always takes):

  curl -sS -i -X POST 'https://spark-leaderboard.saras-fdtta.workers.dev/board/nonet' \
    -H 'Origin: https://spark-online.space' -H 'content-type: application/json' \
    -d '{"runs":[{"name":"ZZZ","ms":99000,"id":"probe-s185-a"}],"focus":"ZZZ"}'

Read the verdict from the status line: **200 with other names in `rows`** → server healthy and populated, so the client is the fault (go back to STEP 1). **200 with only ZZZ** → server healthy but EMPTY: nobody's runs have ever landed. **500 `{"error":"server error"}`** → a D1 table the worker queries does not exist — almost certainly `seen_runs`, and that is the bug. **503 `IP_SALT unset`** → the secret was lost. **403 `forbidden`** → the Origin allowlist (`worker.js:39`). Re-send the identical body WITHOUT the `id` field: if that one succeeds and the id-carrying one 500s, the missing table is `seen_runs` and it is proven.

⚠ Then run the GET, which touches only `players`: `curl -s 'https://spark-leaderboard.saras-fdtta.workers.dev/board/nonet'` — it separates a missing `seen_runs` from a missing `players`. Recovery for either is one command from `server/leaderboard/README.md:110`: `npx wrangler d1 execute spark-leaderboard --remote --file=./schema.sql` (every statement is IF NOT EXISTS, so it is safe to re-run), followed by `npx wrangler deploy`.
